direction: Replace the failed 4–8 point deletions with large-neighbourhood ruin-and-recreate involving 24–40 points at once: pick either a random direction, a deepest-hole direction, or a highest-contact-degree point as a cap centre, delete the 24, 32, or 40 points most aligned with that centre (optionally also deleting their contact neighbours), keep the remaining points fixed initially, and reinsert the deleted points one at a time in random order, where each insertion is chosen by sampling at least 16384 random unit vectors, taking the 8 candidates minimising the maximum cosine to the current set, locally optimising each candidate on the sphere against the current set with an annealed softmax objective, and inserting the best result. After all points are reinserted, jointly relax only points within cosine \(>0.75\) of a reinserted point for a few hundred LSE steps, then run full refinement and LP polish; cycle through cap sizes and centres, because deleting a whole cap rewires a large connected piece of the contact graph instead of asking a few jammed points to find holes that do not exist in the intact configuration.

idea: N-homotopy alternating overshoot (add 1-3 deepest-hole points, hard-refine, delete highest-load points) and undershoot (delete 8-18 highest-load points, polish small code, regrow by deepest-hole insertion) cycles from the best 168-point descendant.
direction: Use an \(N\)-homotopy through oversqueezed and undersized codes rather than perturbing \(N=168\) directly: for the overshoot branch, add 1–3 points at iteratively optimised deepest holes to make \(N=169,170,171\), refine the enlarged code hard even though its maximum cosine will be worse, then delete the point with the largest contact load (contact count at tolerance \(10^{-3}\) plus summed positive excess over \(0.80\)) and refine the resulting 168-point code with LSE plus LP; for the undershoot branch, delete the 8–18 highest-load points, polish the resulting \(N=150\)–\(160\) code to its own optimum, and grow it back to 168 by repeated deepest-hole insertion followed by short joint refinements after every 2–4 insertions. Alternate overshoot and undershoot cycles and seed each cycle from the best 168-point descendant, since pressure from extra points or freedom from missing points can force a global rearrangement that is invisible to fixed-\(N\) local moves.

idea: Quaternionic 7x24 orbit search with cyclic 14x12/21x8 variants, annealed symmetric Adam followed by symmetry-breaking noise plus full LSE and LP polish.
direction: Search a symmetry-reduced orbit ansatz, then break the symmetry: represent unit quaternions by \(4\times4\) left-multiplication matrices and take the 24 Hurwitz units \((\pm1,0,0,0)\) and permutations/signs plus \((\pm\tfrac12,\pm\tfrac12,\pm\tfrac12,\pm\tfrac12)\) as a finite subgroup of SO(4); choose 7 generic seed points on \(S^3\), expand each seed under all 24 group elements to obtain exactly \(7\cdot24=168\) points, and optimise only the 28 seed coordinates with row-normalised annealed log-sum-exp (beta \(30\to500\), tangent gradient, several random seed inits and seeds chosen near the incumbent’s deepest holes). Also try the factorisations \(14\times12\) and \(21\times8\) with cyclic/dihedral actions if time permits, but prioritise the quaternionic \(7\times24\) family. After each symmetric optimum is found, release it by adding tangent noise of sizes \(0.005,0.015,0.03\), run the ordinary full 168-point LSE refinement and trust-region LP polish, and keep both the symmetric score and the symmetry-broken descendants; this tests whether the irregular incumbent is missing a group-orbit structure and uses that structure as a genuinely different starting basin rather than another perturbation of the record.

idea: Diversity-preserving tabu basin walk with contact-hash archive, worse-accepting kicks and Procrustes-aligned cap crossover plus hole repair and LP polish.
direction: Run a diversity-preserving population/tabu basin walk instead of always restarting from the single incumbent: maintain an archive of 6–10 LP-polished local optima distinguished by a hash of their contact adjacency at tolerance \(10^{-4}\) and by their sorted pair-cosine histogram, initialise it from the record plus strongly kicked and hole-reinserted variants, and repeatedly select a parent from the archive (not always the best), generate offspring either by a moderately worse-accepting kick with acceptance threshold up to \(+2\times10^{-4}\) in maximum cosine or by memetic crossover, and insert an offspring only if its contact-graph hash is novel or its score improves the archive. For crossover, align two parents by an SO(4) Procrustes/Kabsch rotation, choose a random unit direction, take the points of the aligned second parent lying in a cap containing roughly one third to one half of the points, replace the nearest points of the first parent by them, repair near-duplicates by deepest-hole reinsertion, then refine and LP-polish; this permits walking through slightly worse but topologically distinct jammed configurations and recombining partial structures, directly addressing the elitist collapse back to the incumbent basin.

idea: Prune high contact-degree points to unjammed smaller codes then beam-search reinsertion with hole refinement and short annealed LSE polish.
direction: Use an $N$-changing homotopy with beam-search reinsertion rather than perturbing all 168 points: prune the incumbent successively to $N=160$–$166$ by removing the highest-degree/contact-stress points, fully LSE+LP polish each smaller code (which has a strictly lower achievable max cosine), then reinsert points one at a time, each time generating $20$–$50$ candidate holes from $30$k random sphere samples plus local hole refinement, keeping a beam of the best $6$–$10$ partial configurations after a short $200$-step annealed polish at each size, and finally LP-polish the best few $168$-point completions; this forces genuinely different contact topologies because intermediate codes are unjammed and the reinsertion order, not just positions, is searched.

idea: Hopf-fiber symmetric search with low-dimensional Adam over base radius, base phase and fiber offsets for N<=8 partitions then symmetry-breaking anneal and LP polish filtered by contact-degree variance.
direction: Search a Hopf-fibration ansatz from scratch, a regular structure absent from the amorphous incumbent: write $S^3$ points via a base point on $S^2$ and a fiber angle, choose partitions such as $14$ fibers $\times12$, $21\times8$, $12\times14$, and $28\times6$ points, parameterize only the base spherical code, per-fiber phase, fiber radius/tilt, and within-fiber angular spacings, optimize this low-dimensional symmetric family with Adam on a high-$\beta$ LSE objective for several thousand cheap steps and multiple random seeds, then release all $168$ points with tiny symmetry-breaking noise ($10^{-3}$–$10^{-2}$), anneal, and LP-polish; accept the run only if its post-break contact-degree variance is lower than the incumbent's, since the goal is a near-regular contact graph rather than another copy of the record basin.

idea: Target-feasibility homotopy lowering cosine targets with two-shell ReLU penalty and Riemannian Adam plus hub-rotation restarts and LP polish.
direction: Replace max-normalized LSE (whose gradient vanishes back into the same optimum) by a target-feasibility homotopy: for targets $t=0.8592,0.8590,0.8587,0.8584,\dots$ minimize the explicit penalty $\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{relu}(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t)^2+0.1\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{relu}(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t+0.002)^2$ over all pairs with Riemannian Adam, starting each stage from the previous minimizer and lowering $t$ only when the violating-pair count and penalty plateau; whenever a stage reaches near-zero violation, LP-polish and record it, otherwise restart that stage from the best-penalty point with the worst violating hub points randomly rotated by $0.05$–$0.15$ rad—this puts direct pressure on the second shell (pairs ranked $500$–$1500$) that LP ignores until they become maximal.

idea: Random-seed Hurwitz 7x24 and cyclic 14x12/21x8/12x14/8x21 orbit search with annealed symmetric Adam, orbit-wise release then noisy full LSE anneal and LP polish gated by contact-topology novelty.
direction: Run a genuinely symmetry-constrained search from random seeds rather than from `best.npy`: enumerate factorizations $168=7\cdot24$ using the 24 Hurwitz left-multiplication matrices, $14\cdot12$ and $21\cdot8$ using block-diagonal cyclic rotations $C_m$ with several frequency pairs $(1,k)$, and optimize only the $7$, $14$, or $21$ unit seed vectors with Adam on the log-sum-exp objective, annealing $\beta=20\to800$ and learning rate $0.02\to0.001$ for 1500–3000 steps per restart over many short restarts, promoting the best few symmetry classes to long runs. Then break symmetry in stages—first release one orbit at a time while freezing the others, then add tangential noise of sizes $0.005$, $0.02$, and $0.05$ and run the full unconstrained LSE anneal followed by the trust-region LP polish—and accept a result only if its contact adjacency at slack $<10^{-6}$ differs substantially from the incumbent, always retaining the LP-polished loaded best as a fallback.

idea: Build several-thousand-point algebraic pool from 24-cell/D4 shells and 600-cell plus optimized random rotations, then thresholded conflict-graph randomized greedy independent-set with 1-for-2/2-for-3 swaps and void completion plus LSE/LP polish.
direction: Search over algebraic candidate pools and discrete packings to import structure the amorphous incumbent lacks: generate several thousand unit vectors from rotated copies of the 24-cell, 600-cell, $D_4$ shells such as permutations of $(\pm1,\pm1,0,0)/\sqrt2$ and $(\pm1,0,0,0)$, Hurwitz-unit orbits, and pairs of 600-cells related by optimized random orthogonal transforms; for thresholds $t$ binary-searched around $0.850$–$0.8593$, build the conflict graph with edges where cosine exceeds $t$ and run randomized greedy maximum-independent-set with local $1$-for-$2$ and $2$-for-$3$ swaps to try to select 168 mutually compatible pool points, iterating over rotations and pool mixtures. idea: Batched de novo Riemannian-Adam homotopy over LSE losses with beta 5→1000, LR/noise lanes and periodic cull-and-clone selection, followed by high-beta single refinement and trust-region LP squeeze.
direction: Perform batched de novo global optimization with no record seeding except as a final safety comparison: maintain a tensor of $B=16$ independent configurations of shape $(B,168,4)$, vectorize all Gram matrices, and minimize a homotopy family from Riesz-type energies $\sum_{i<j}(x_i^\top x_j)_+^{s}$ or LSE losses with $\beta$ increasing from $5$ to $1000$, using Riemannian Adam with several learning-rate/temperature lanes for thousands of steps; every $\sim1000$ steps, rank the batch, discard or reinitialize the worst half from perturbed copies of the better half plus fresh random codes, and continue so CPU time buys many basins rather than one long trajectory. Take the best three final configurations, run individual high-$\beta$ LSE refinement and the LP polish in the last 30–40 seconds, and return the better of those and the LP-polished loaded incumbent.

idea: Rigidity/stress-guided basin hopping that breaks the jammed contact graph with floppy-mode kicks and overload surgery plus tabu search.
direction: Use rigidity/stress-guided topology flips of the incumbent: extract active contacts with slack $<10^{-7}$, build an orthonormal tangent basis $B_i\in\mathbb R^{4\times3}$ for every point, assemble the contact rigidity matrix $R\in\mathbb R^{p\times504}$ whose $(i,j)$ row contains $B_i^\top x_j$ and $B_j^\top x_i$, and compute its SVD (feasible at this size) together with LP dual stresses for the active pairs. Generate kicks along random combinations of the 10–20 smallest-singular-value modes, supplemented by deleting/repelling the highest-stress overloaded points of degree 8–9 and their contact neighbours, with amplitudes $0.03$–$0.15$ rad chosen adaptively so that at least 30 old contacts acquire slack $>10^{-3}$ while the kicked maximum stays below $\sim0.90$; then re-anneal with LSE and LP-polish, storing a hash of the sorted contact-degree sequence and quantized top cosines in a tabu archive so the walk cannot return to the incumbent graph. This directly attacks the jammed, degree-imbalanced active set instead of making isotropic noise.

idea: Spectral-bottleneck twists plus degree-balanced ridge-walking to leave the over-isostatic jammed vertex for a more uniform-contact basin.
